subject: log data vs raw data using MLR

messages.author: ea16eb8f0785b8d3
messages.subject: log data vs raw data using MLR
parts:
I'm working on a multigroup SEM model. My data is not normally distributed, I read here that that is not an issue and I can use a robust MLR method. However, when I do this the model is not identified and I get a warning that some variances are much larger than others. If I do a log transformation before running a ML estimation things work just fine. 

What would be the best way to go about this?

Note that I have NAs in my data so there are some estimation methods I can't use.

Thank you,

Sil

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: log data vs raw data using MLR
parts:
That doesn't sound like an identification issue, but a nonconvergence issue.  It is better to rescale some variables by multiplying or dividing by 10 or 100 or 1000 (whatever is meaningful).  For example, a proportion variable can be rescaled to a percentage-points variable by multiplying by 100.  Or income can be expressed in thousands of currency-units (e.g., dollars) by dividing by 1000.
